name: Mokokchung Town
description: District headquarters and cultural capital of the Ao Naga tribe, known as the Land of Pioneers, with vibrant markets, churches, and hill views.
facts: Elevation about 1,325 m
Cultural heartland of Ao Nagas
Famous for Moatsu Festival in May
Sources: Wikipedia, official district site

name: Ungma Village
description: Oldest and one of the largest Ao Naga villages, considered the birthplace of the Ao people, featuring traditional morungs, log drums, and Baptist church.
facts: Located about 3-10 km from Mokokchung town
Preserves ancient log drums and Ao traditions
Divided into Yimpang and Yimlang khels
Sources: mokokchung.nic.in, Wikipedia

name: Longkhum Village
description: Highest Ao village with panoramic views, rhododendrons, Mata Yimkong viewpoint, stone bridge (Longlangba), and folklore that souls stay behind after a visit.
facts: Elevation about 1,846 m
Known for cherry blossom festival and rhododendrons
Hosts Cherry Blossom Festival
Sources: Wikipedia, mokokchung.nic.in

name: Mopungchuket Village
description: Designated rural tourism village, one of the cleanest in Nagaland, famous for Jina-Etiben love story towers, Süngkotenem Park with mystical lake, museum, and wooden sculptures.
facts: Declared rural tourism village in 2007
Home to oldest rural museum (1956) and first tea garden in Nagaland
Features log drums and traditional morung
Sources: mokokchung.nic.in, Wikipedia

name: Mokokchung District Museum
description: Museum in the Arts and Cultural Complex showcasing Ao Naga artefacts, weapons, traditional attire, jewellery, and tribal history.
facts: Houses Ao warrior shields, shawls, and everyday artefacts
Located in Mokokchung town
Sources: tourism guides, official listings

name: Ao Baptist Church (Baptist Mother Church)
description: One of the largest Baptist churches in Nagaland and a historical landmark central to Ao Naga Christian life and literacy.
facts: Nicknamed Mother Church or Mokokchung Church
Central to Ao community and festivals
Sources: tourism sites, local descriptions

name: Mokokchung Park (Town Park)
description: Hillside town park above the center offering gardens, viewpoints, and a serene escape amid the hills.
facts: Popular for picnics and valley views
Located just above the town center
Sources: official and tourism listings

name: Langpangkong Caves
description: Limestone caves in the Langpangkong range near Tuli and Changtongya, associated with legend of an Ahom king taking refuge, with nearby Fusen Kei and Mongzu Ki.
facts: Located between Dikhu and Tzula river valleys
About 30-40 km from Mokokchung near Tuli
Coordinates approximate; Sources: district and tourism sites

name: Chuchuyimlang Village
description: Large Ao village known for hosting Moatsu Festival with neighboring tribes, traditional handicrafts, and cultural performances.
facts: About 30 km from Mokokchung on NH61
Famous for Moatsu celebrations open to other tribes
Sources: Wikipedia, tourism guides

name: Dikhu River (Mokokchung section)
description: Scenic river section in the district ideal for picnics, nature walks, and views near Langpangkong and Tuli areas.
facts: Important for local ecology and tourism
Near caves and villages
Coordinates approximate for district section

name: Wokha Town
description: District headquarters and cultural capital of the Lotha Naga tribe, known as the Land of Plenty, with hill views, markets, and access to Mount Tiyi and Doyang.
facts: Elevation about 1,313 m
Name means 'census' in Lotha
Famous for Tokhu Emong Festival in November
Sources: Wikipedia, wokha.nic.in

name: Mount Tiyi
description: Highest peak in Wokha district (~1,969 m), known as the Mountain of Life and abode of departed souls in Lotha folklore, with rhododendrons, nature trails, and panoramic views.
facts: Elevation about 1,969 m
Believed to be repository of ancestors' souls
Popular for trekking and rhododendrons
Coordinates approximate from Wikimapia; Sources: tourism guides, Wikipedia

name: Doyang Hydro Electric Project and Reservoir
description: 75 MW hydroelectric dam and large scenic reservoir on the Doyang River, major tourist attraction with water sports potential and surrounding hills.
facts: Commissioned in 2000, capacity 75 MW
Only major river dam in Nagaland
About 38 km from Wokha town
Sources: Wikipedia (Doyang), Global Energy Monitor, official

name: Pangti Village
description: Large Lotha Naga village near Doyang Reservoir, globally famous as the Amur Falcon roosting capital of the world during October–November migration.
facts: Hosts one of the largest congregations of Amur Falcons
Elevation about 902 m
Conservation success story with community involvement
Sources: Wikipedia, tourism sites, Key Biodiversity Areas

name: Totsu Cliff (Mount Totsu)
description: Scenic cliff and mountain viewpoint offering panoramic valley vistas, associated with local folklore of guardians (giant snake and crab), suitable for rock climbing and photography.
facts: About 25 km from Wokha town, altitude around 1,250 m
Ideal for rock climbing and sunset views
Coordinates approximate; Sources: NativePlanet, tourism guides

name: Liphanyan Governor’s Camp
description: Riverside camp and picnic spot in the foothills along the Doyang River, popular for trekking, angling, and nature escapes near Wokha.
facts: Accessible from Dimapur (~43 km) or Wokha
Ideal for rafting and angling
Coordinates approximate; Sources: tourism guides, NativePlanet

name: Vankhosung
description: Cultural and spiritual area near Wokha town, home to the historic Vankhosung Baptist Church (birthplace of Baptist faith among Lothas) and traditional community spaces.
facts: Epicenter of Baptist Christianity in Wokha district
Near Wokha town agglomeration
Sources: tourism sites, local history

name: Baghty Valley
description: Lush agricultural valley known for passion fruit cultivation, scenic hills, and peaceful rural landscapes in Wokha district.
facts: Known for large-scale passion fruit farming
Offers panoramic vistas near Totsu area
Coordinates approximate; Sources: tourism guides
